facts.fact: SERNIE's director writes that since its creation in 1991 SERNIE staff have recorded learners in schools on paper forms carried physically to Kinshasa for central data entry, with delays that leave the data out of date; no date is given for the statement, so the document's publication date is used.
facts.system: SERNIE learner records (paper forms, central entry)

facts.fact: EDUSER is a digital enrolment system in which SERNIE staff, on their usual school visits, register each learner by app at local level (state-issued identity document, age, sex, disability, maternal status, grade), replacing paper forms; the first test in schools was a three-week pilot in April 2026, per SERNIE's director.
The April 2026 EDUSER pilot was run in 20 primary schools of Kasai province, per SERNIE's director.

SERNIE teams registered 8,634 learners (4,509 girls, 4,125 boys) in 20 primary schools of Kasai province in a three-week EDUSER pilot in April 2026, described by SERNIE's director as only a pilot phase; no national total of schools is given.

The document states that ownership and use of EDUSER rest with the DRC education ministry, operated by SERNIE, the ministry's public service for individual learner data, with technical support from CGA Technologies (a Corus company); no date is given, so the publication date is used.
The document says the EDUSER pilot was funded but its future is uncertain without continued investment, and does not name the funder; no date is given, so the publication date is used.

In April 2026 SERNIE completed the first test of EDUSER in schools, a three-week pilot in 20 primary schools of Kasai, after cascade training of SERNIE staff at national, provincial and local levels; the director says it laid the basis for a national rollout, which is not funded.
